subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed `sessions_spawn` keep returning `accepted` and surface Docker startup failures asynchronously, or preflight enough sandbox startup work to reject before returning?
rationale: That choice affects the public async spawn contract, gateway wait behavior, session lifecycle projection, subagent list/status output, and overlap with the broader lifecycle-event work.

options.title: Terminalize Async Startup Failures
options.body: Keep the accepted response contract and make Docker startup failures visible as typed terminal state in logs, session history, subagent status, and waits.

options.title: Preflight Before Accept
options.body: Move enough sandbox initialization before the accepted response to fail fast, accepting extra spawn latency and compatibility review for existing callers.

options.title: Defer To Lifecycle Tracker
options.body: Leave this sandbox-specific issue open while maintainers settle the broader lifecycle contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58776.

recommendation.title: Terminalize Async Startup Failures
recommendation.body: Keep the accepted response contract and make Docker startup failures visible as typed terminal state in logs, session history, subagent status, and waits.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent adjacent lifecycle work make this the best available owner for the spawn/sandbox contract choice.
